issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares Ride.abbreviation as type String, but the solution implementation uses a char for the abbreviation attribute and for all constructors/getters that expose it. This is a cross-artifact type mismatch: students reading the UML will implement abbreviation as String (and the exercise explicitly requires constructors with parameters in the same order and types as in the UML), while the provided solution uses char. This mismatch affects attribute type, constructor parameter types and getter signatures, and will confuse students about the intended type or cause test mismatches.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the abbreviation type consistent across artifacts. Either update the UML/problem statement to declare abbreviation as char (if a single character is intended) or update the solution (and any templates/tests) to use String for the abbreviation attribute, constructor parameters, and getter return types. Prefer updating the solution to use String to match the UML and the explicit instructions in the problem statement about attribute types and constructor parameter order.
